title: char.yml
description: The committed configuration for one charkit workspace. Specified in docs/PLAN.md §4. This schema is authoritative: the serde structs in crates/core mirror it, and the fixtures under tests/fixtures are what keep the two honest. Rules that can be decided from the value in front of you live here; rules needing a second part of the document, or the filesystem, live in `char config verify` (PLAN.md §5). Every pattern below is lookaround-free, because char validates with a Rust regex engine that has no lookahead.

version.description: Config format version. Required — a config with no version is bad_config, since the whole point of the key is to exist before it is needed (PLAN.md §4.1).

components.description: A component is a named thing that may have source to check (`checks:`), a process to run (`run:`), or both. Two axes, not two kinds of thing (PLAN.md §4.1).

commands.description: Repo-local verbs char dispatches but does not define (PLAN.md §4.5). Remaining argv passes through untouched and the child's exit code is returned verbatim.

allOf.$comment: A commands: entry may not shadow a built-in verb — it would silently break the one guarantee the project exists to provide (PLAN.md §4.5).

workspaces.description: Paths that are separate workspaces, each with its own complete char.yml, excluded from this one (PLAN.md §4.6). A nested workspace inherits nothing. A root that is nothing but this key is legal.

secrets.description: Environment variable name to a secret reference. The URI scheme selects the provider; the rest is `${ref}` (PLAN.md §4.7). A reference, never a value.

secret_providers.description: A provider is a command that prints one secret to stdout — never an SDK integration (PLAN.md §4.7).

name.description: Component, check, port and exclusive names. `:` is reserved, because check ids are derived as `<component>:<check>` and `needs:` tells a component from a check id by the colon alone (PLAN.md §4.1).

scheme.description: A provider name is a URI scheme, so it uses the scheme grammar rather than the name grammar — `_` is legal in a name and illegal in a scheme, so `aws_sm:` would be a provider that can never be referenced (PLAN.md §4.7).

relPath.description: A path relative to the workspace root. The schema rejects a leading `/`, any `..` segment, and the `.` / `./` spellings of the root — one idea, one spelling, so a glob cannot match in one config and not in another. `config verify` owns the rest, because only verify can normalise `a/../../b` or resolve a symlink (PLAN.md §5).

command.description: A command string. Argv-split by default, respecting quotes; `shell: true` on the entry opts it into shell interpretation instead (PLAN.md §4.1). `${files}` is not available here — only a file-scoped check has a file set, and a silently empty expansion is the failure PLAN.md §4.1's empty-set rule exists to prevent.

allOf.$comment: `${files}` is legal only on a check's cmd:/fix: (PLAN.md §4.5).
`${env.NAME}` is legal only inside an env: block (PLAN.md §4.4).
No expression language: `${env.NAME ?? "default"}` is rejected by the schema, not merely undocumented (PLAN.md §4.4).

checkCommand.description: A check's `cmd:` or `fix:`. Identical to a command string except that `${files}` is available — and must stand alone as a whole token, because the placeholder expands to n argv elements and n arguments cannot be pasted inside one (PLAN.md §4.1).

envValue.description: An env: value. The four substitutions apply, plus a bare `${env.NAME}` read — unset is bad_config, naming the variable (PLAN.md §4.4). `${files}` is excluded: it expands to separate argv elements, which has no meaning inside one env value.

env.description: Additive over the inherited environment — a child needing `$HOME` already has it (PLAN.md §4.5).

secretGrant.description: Names granted to this entry and nowhere else. Least privilege, and `grep -n "secrets:"` answers "what can reach this token" (PLAN.md §4.7). Every name must be declared in the top-level `secrets:` — checked by `config verify`, which is the only thing that can see both.

secretRef.description: `<scheme>://<ref>`. The scheme selects a declared provider; everything after it is substituted into that provider's `${ref}` as a single argv element.

cmd.description: Must contain `${ref}` — a provider cmd without it can never resolve anything (PLAN.md §4.4). There is deliberately no `shell:` key here: PLAN.md §4.7 rule 1 exists to keep `${ref}` out of a shell.

setupStep.description: One step of `char init`. The object form exists so a single step can opt into shell interpretation — visible in the diff, so a reviewer can see exactly where shell semantics are live (PLAN.md §4.1).

shell.description: Opt this entry into shell interpretation, where `|| true`, pipes, redirection and inline assignments work. It covers every command string in the entry it appears on. Not a security boundary — an ergonomic escape in a config you already trust (PLAN.md §4.1).

ready.description: Exactly one kind key, plus an optional timeout in seconds (default 60). A mapping with two kind keys is bad_config rather than a precedence rule nobody would remember (PLAN.md §6.0). Omitted defaults to `{none: true}`.

tcp.description: Ready when the port accepts a connection. A declared port NAME, never a number — a number would be the pre-claim port, which is never the one the service is on.

log.description: Ready when this unanchored regex matches the service's stdout.

exec.description: Ready when this command exits 0. Dispatched like any other command string, so the same substitution rules apply.

none.description: Ready immediately on spawn — the service is fire-and-forget.

ports.description: Port name to the port the service itself listens on. char claims a host port from this workspace's block and maps it; `${port.NAME}` always resolves to the host port (PLAN.md §4.1). The namespace is workspace-global, not per component, so two components may not declare the same name — `config verify` owns that check, since it needs the whole document.

needs.description: A component name means the service must be running; a check id (`core:build`) means that check must have passed in this run. The two forms are told apart by the colon (PLAN.md §4.1). Ordering, never a build graph.

ownsSelector.description: A docker filter expression. Every selector is stamped with `${workspace.id}`, which is what lets `char clean` evaluate a commands: entry's declaration ad hoc (PLAN.md §4.5). Declared selectors may use the id alone; char's own filters use both labels (PLAN.md §2.3.1).

ownsFiles.description: Paths this entry created, removed only by `char clean --artifacts` (PLAN.md §6.1). They cost disk but leak nothing machine-global, and deleting them makes the next init pay a full reinstall.

ownsRelease.description: External resources char did not create and cannot reclaim — a database on a shared server, a cloud namespace. Recorded at `char init` and reported by `char status`, NEVER executed (PLAN.md §6.1). Takes no secrets grant anywhere, which is what keeps char.db free of secret references.

ownsRun.description: What `run:` started (PLAN.md §6.0). The three owns: key sets are not the same set.

ownsComponent.description: What `setup:` created. No runtime handles, so no containers, networks, images or ports here (PLAN.md §6.0).

ownsCommand.description: A selector, not a record — `char clean` evaluates it against docker and the filesystem, because a command runs ad hoc and has no "while it was up" window to record against. `ports:` is not available: the block is already claimed by `char init` (PLAN.md §4.5).

fix.description: Run instead of `cmd:` under `char check --fix`. Checks that declare none are skipped by that flag (PLAN.md §3.2).

timeout.description: Seconds. Defaults to `check_timeout` from ~/.char/config.toml, itself 900 — a check with no deadline is a hung merge gate (PLAN.md §4.1).

scope.description: `file` (the default) passes `${files}`; `component` always runs over the whole component. An end-to-end suite scoped to two changed files tests nothing (PLAN.md §4.1).

exclusive.description: Machine-wide mutexes, never shared. Acquired before cpu-slots and in sorted name order, which is what makes a cross-workspace deadlock impossible rather than unlikely (PLAN.md §4.3).

in.description: Run this check inside a running container, via an exec char builds itself from the file list and project name it already owns. Names a compose SERVICE, not a component — a component's compose files routinely define several. Implies `needs:` on the enclosing component, which must be `driver: compose` (PLAN.md §4.1).

allOf.$comment: `shell: true` with `${files}` is unrepresentable, not warned about: a filename may contain `;` or `$(…)`, so under a shell anyone who can push a branch has code execution on every machine that runs char check on it (PLAN.md §4.1, traps.md).
A scope: component check containing ${files} says two opposite things, and quietly honouring one of them is how you get a suite that appears to run and covers nothing (PLAN.md §4.1).
A check with in: may not be granted secrets: — the only way to hand a value to an exec'd process is `-e KEY=value`, which puts it in argv (PLAN.md §4.1, ARCHITECTURE.md §1.8).

driver.description: Two drivers only. No vendor-named drivers (PLAN.md §6).

file.description: compose only. A list, because repos commonly already run base plus override and the resolve step must receive the same file set they do (PLAN.md §6.0).

cmd.description: command only. Spawned detached in its own process group.

stop.description: command only. Optional; the default is killpg — SIGTERM, 10s grace, then SIGKILL, unconditionally (PLAN.md §6).

root.description: Where this component's source lives. NOT a working directory — every check runs from the workspace root, and `${files}` paths are workspace-relative (PLAN.md §4.1). It scopes `match:` and resolves executables for `config verify`.

match.description: Globs, workspace-relative, that decide which changed files select this component. `char check --all-files` sets `${files}` from these instead of from the diff.

setup.description: What `char init` runs. A single step or a sequence. char is idempotent in its own state; whether re-running a step is safe is a property of the repo's commands (PLAN.md §4.1).

checks.description: Check ids are derived as `<component>:<check>` — never written by hand, so they cannot drift, collide or be typo'd (PLAN.md §4.1).

help.description: One line, for `char --help` and the managed AGENTS.md block.

stdio.description: `pipe` lets char scrub the child's output; `inherit` preserves its TTY, so colours and interactive prompts work. Default is inferred — pipe when the entry grants secrets, inherit otherwise — but inference is wrong in both directions, so the repo may say. `--json` overrides this and forces pipe (PLAN.md §4.5).
